new_kent_parade.status: OSM frontage lines with LiDAR-constrained overall massing. Ground-floor shopfronts, signs and first-/second-floor openings are an illustrative street elevation requested on 21 August 2026, not a measured facade survey.

traffic.note: No DfT count point. County Street is a residential street serving the terrace and is not a through route; its flow is small beside the A201 but it is the nearer road to the front elevation.

sources.evidence_status: reported operational; visible plume documented in supplied site media
sources.position_provenance: OSM address interpolation and the POI tagged 173 New Kent Road; rear-wall mounting assumed. The same plot rear used for the 2025 wind-sector analysis. Not surveyed.

sources.evidence_status: photo-observed context outlet; premise assignment and geometry provisional
sources.position_provenance: A nearby outlet is visible in the 9 August photographs. The current point is placed behind the OSM Chicky Wiki POI at E -40.7 only as a context marker. The outlet-to-premise link, rear-wall position and height are not surveyed.

weather_stations.label: Tempest weather station
weather_stations.position_provenance: WGS84 GPS position supplied by the site owner on 12 August 2026; not surveyed. Raw local position is retained in east_m/north_m.
weather_stations.render_position_provenance: User/photo-corrected on 13 August 2026: north of and aligned with unit 1, on the western wall section between the greenhouse and south wall. The universal mount is anchored on that west wall and projects to the sensor head.
weather_stations.height_provenance: Sensor head approximately five feet (1.52 m) above the local terrace deck, confirmed by the site owner on 13 August 2026; approximate and not used analytically.

receptor_homes.label: Intervening neighbour between 74–75 and 81a
receptor_homes.provenance: OSM footprint and Environment Agency 1 m LiDAR levels, with photo-informed architectural detail from the 19 August 2026 visit. the site owner clarified on 21 August that this is the intervening neighbour, not the 81a host; approximate, not surveyed.

receptor_homes.label: 81a County Street · raised rear garden over a pitched solar roof
receptor_homes.screening_note: The panels are fixed flush to the pitched roof on the source-facing south side of the bamboo screen, so they carry the roof's own 30 degree angle. The garden is set back on the higher 8.20 m deck to the north. The screen therefore interrupts the lower direct view toward the 173 flue.
receptor_homes.house_relationship_note: The light-brick gabled 81a house keeps its screen-side wall fixed and extends west to share a party wall with the adjoining house. Its broad south rear wall carries two large windows so it reads as a house rather than a detached blank slab. The bamboo run still terminates at the house instead of wrapping around or continuing across the solar roof.
receptor_homes.provenance: The 81/81a OSM plot and Environment Agency 1 m LiDAR context. The pitched solar roof, house, terminating screen and raised garden are read from the 19 August photographs and set out on the plot grid after the site owner's 21 August corrections; approximate, not surveyed.

receptor_homes.label: Neighbouring plot west of 81a · matching house format
receptor_homes.provenance: OSM plot and LiDAR context, drawn to the same format as 81a on the site owner's 21 August note that the two houses match; approximate, not surveyed.

receptor_homes.label: Adjacent private home and roof garden · context only
receptor_homes.deployment_note: The private home and its planted roof garden are context only. Unit 3 is not deployed here: it is on the communal gallery rail to the west.
receptor_homes.provenance: OSM/LiDAR context with the photo-informed private home, glazing, roof garden and planting from the 19 August installation sequence; approximate, not surveyed.

receptor_homes.label: Communal access gallery · unit 3
receptor_homes.position_note: One communal gallery, south of the private home and running north-south with its safety rail facing east. The planted roof garden to the north is private and separate.
receptor_homes.absence_note: The gallery stays on one level, with rails on every open edge and no steps.
receptor_homes.provenance: The 19 August photographs establish the communal metal-bar gallery, its concrete canopy and the lit render wall behind it. the site owner's 21 August mark-up places it south of the private home; his WGS84 fix that day (51.49446765756895, -0.09250583738303685) falls about 7 m north of the drawn position and is retained as raw provenance only. Not surveyed.

colocation.label: 5-9 August co-location: four outdoor units
colocation.status: Four outdoor units approximately five feet above the south-facing terrace/deck. From the right-hand end of the primary view: units 1, 2, 3 and 4. Spacing remains illustrative. Unit 5 was indoors throughout.

5.environment: indoor - rear bedroom, inside the home
5.note: Indoor-model instrument, indoors throughout the export window. Confirmed by the site owner and independently supported by the data: it lags the outdoor units by about an hour, its temperature and PM2.5 ranges are damped, and it retains 85% of their 0.3 um particle count while reporting 44% of their PM2.5 mass - the coarse-mode removal expected across a building envelope. It is not a faulty outdoor unit.

deployment.label: installed deployment · 19 August 2026
deployment.status: Units 1 and 4 share the timber rail beside Tempest; unit 2 is on the farther 81a plot's bamboo screen beyond the intervening neighbour, with solar panels on the lower source-facing belt and the garden higher behind; unit 3 is on the communal deck-access gallery's east-facing metal safety rail, opposite the adjacent private roof garden, at the site owner's 21 August GPS fix; unit 5 remains indoors. Positions are photographically confirmed but approximate rather than surveyed.
